questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

She nodded her

A-head, and unapologetically shrugged

B-her shoulders while pointing to the

C-fine receipt she had just handed to me
questions.solution:
To nod = lower and raise one's head slightly and briefly showing agreement.

Clearly, A (head) must be first. Option 1) *ABC *is the correct answer.

***She nodded her head, and unapologetically shrugged her shoulders while pointing to the fine receipt she had just handed to me.***

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

The king said, “Alas! Our enemies are too strong.”

options.text: The king said that their enemies were too strong.
The king exclaimed sadly that their enemies were too strong.
The king was sad because the enemies were too strong.
The enemies were too strong for the king.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The king exclaimed sadly that their enemies were too strong.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

While changing the narration of an exclamatory sentence, we need to follow the steps given below-

 
• An exclamatory sentence expresses a state of joy, sorrow, or wonder, to change them into Indirect Speech, specific words (i.e. exclaimed with joy, exclaimed with sorrow, exclaimed with surprise, etc.) are added to the sentence.
 
• Put "that" between the reporting and reported speeches. (it is optional to put "that" between the reporting and reported speech)
 
• Present indefinite tense in direct speech is changed into past indefinite tense in indirect speech.
 
• **'Our' **will be changed into **'their'.**

Thus, the sentence becomes: *The king exclaimed sadly that their enemies were too strong.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

He refused them donation.

options.text: They were refused donation by him.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They were refused donation by him.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and '**He**' is the subject and '**them**' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject '**He**' of the active voice becomes the object (him), the object '**them**' becomes the subject 'they'.
 
• The passive format "were + V3 (refused)" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the past simple tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

In developing

P: and poor schooling opportunities,

Q: countries, due to high poverty

R: child labour is still prevalent
questions.solution:
*Developing *is an adjective and therefore, must be followed by a noun. Thus, P (starts with **and**) can't be first. Rule out 1). A sentence can't end with a comma. Thus, P can't be last either. Rule out 3) and 4). Option 2) *QPR *is the correct answer.

***In developing countries, due to high poverty and poor schooling opportunities, child labour is still prevalent.***

• ​Thus, 'dry' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The Large Hadron Collider is the world's largest and most (1)/ powerful particle collider, the most complex experimental (2)/ facility, and the largest single machine in a world (3)`. No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error is in 3). The correct order of adjectives is *Quantity-Opinion-Size-Shape-Age-Colour-Origin-Material-Type-Purpose. *

*Single = quantity.*

*Largest = size*.

Thus, the sentence is wrong because of the order.

*the **single largest **machine in **the **world.*

Notice that **a **had also been wrongly used in place of **the**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

If I had cared, (1)/ I will buy (2)/ it again. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **'would have bought' **will be there in place of **'will buy'**
 
• What are Third conditional sentences?__

 Third conditional sentences are used to explain that present circumstances would be different if something different had happened in the past.

 We use (had +past participle) in "if clause" and (should have/ could have/would have.. +verb3 form) in "main clause." 

 EXAMPLES:
 
• If you had studied harder, you would have passed the exam. 
 
• If I had known you were sick, I would have visited you in the hospital. 

**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***If I had cared, I would have bought it again.*
